receipt.supersedesClaimsOnly: v1 artifacts and hashes remain immutable; this receipt corrects interpretation of their labels.
corrections: A canonical filename is an unvalidated semantic hypothesis until the exact artifact is identified by at least two distinct AI reviewer identities.
A deterministic corruption probe proves the named geometry change occurred; it does not prove the change is critical or meaning-changing.
Unaltered house-source controls are source baselines, not human-approved or AI-approved craft positives.

protocol.semanticResolution: Retain each free description and choice. A catalog filename becomes an assessment label only when two distinct actual reviewer identities independently agree on object and modifier/action. Disagreement or uncertainty remains unresolved.
protocol.criticalityResolution: For corrupted controls, retain objective probe truth separately. Criticality requires two distinct actual reviewer identities to classify the visible consequence as critical. Geometry corruption alone cannot satisfy this gate.
protocol.leakageBoundary: Packet files expose only opaque IDs, artifact hashes, native size, stratum, free-description prompt, and a hash of withheld stage-two choices. Catalog labels, aliases, choices, control kind, corruption objective, and criticality status remain in the withheld key.

limitations: No AI reviewer or image inspection ran; all semantic and criticality decisions remain unresolved.
The seal is bounded to the preserved accessible history inherited from v1 and does not claim global novelty.
SVG artifacts are inputs only. A runnable campaign must separately freeze rendered evidence, actual reviewer routes, deadlines, and exact stage-one-before-stage-two enforcement.
